hyperedges.label: DaVinci Resolve crash mux/timing factors in 1.mp4

nodes.label: 1.mp4
nodes.rationale: Stream-copied trim (-c:v copy) producing a malformed 10-bit HEVC MP4 with broken timeline; DaVinci Resolve crashes on import due to mux/timing issues rather than resolution or Opus alone.

nodes.label: 1_working.mp4
nodes.rationale: Full libx265 re-encode (CRF 18) with clean MP4 structure (ctts present, colr BT.709, exact 3840x2160 8-bit Main); works in DaVinci Resolve.

nodes.label: colr box
nodes.rationale: Color metadata atom (BT.709 in working file); missing in crash file usually causes color issues not crashes, but signals incomplete remux.

nodes.label: ctts box
nodes.rationale: Composition timestamp table required when B-frames are present; without it presentation order is undefined in MP4 — known NLE/Resolve failure mode for HEVC.

nodes.label: DaVinci Resolve
nodes.rationale: NLE parser less tolerant than ffmpeg/ffprobe of broken HEVC-in-MP4 mux/timing; crashes on 1.mp4 import.

nodes.label: Edit list
nodes.rationale: In 1.mp4 video edit list uses media_time=53925 and duration=27028 (90k timescale) to hide in-GOP start and extra stream-copy frames; Resolve tolerates this poorly.

nodes.label: HEVC Main 10
nodes.rationale: 10-bit Main 10 @ L5.2 High tier with stored height 2176 padding; finicky in some apps and a plausible crash co-factor with broken mux.

nodes.label: Open GOP
nodes.rationale: Stream copy at cut point must grab extra frames from an open GOP, yielding 828 samples vs expected ~810 for ~27s at 29.97 fps.

nodes.label: Opus audio
nodes.rationale: Less likely crash factor here because working file also uses Opus; Option C suggests strip-audio test to isolate HEVC/mux vs audio.

nodes.label: Broken MP4 timeline
nodes.rationale: Most likely Resolve crash cause: container/timing (missing ctts with B-frames, bad edit list, extra samples from open-GOP stream copy), not codec name alone.

nodes.label: libx265 re-encode
nodes.rationale: Preferred fix for Resolve: re-encode with libx265 CRF 18 yuv420p to rebuild clean container timing; safer than stream-copy trim.

nodes.label: -ss after -i trim
nodes.rationale: If video must be stream-copied, put -ss after -i; may still get GOP-edge weirdness — re-encoding remains safer for Resolve.

nodes.label: Stream copy trim
nodes.rationale: ffmpeg -ss before -i with -c:v copy grabs extra open-GOP frames and yields incomplete remux (missing ctts/colr, bad edit list); unsafe for Resolve.
